reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) strongly supports the nano-bridged honeycomb microstructure and its toughening mechanism in Al0.5CrCoFeNi, but none of the evidence involves W-Cu alloys, their thermal transport properties, or any comparison to conventional W-Cu materials. The key premises that the W-Cu system can form such an HEA and will outperform conventional W-Cu materials are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: L-PBF can produce a nano-bridged honeycomb microstructure in a high-entropy alloy
This microstructure provides an excellent combination of strength and toughness via intrinsic toughening
The mechanism involves nano-bridges of dislocations acting as highways for dislocation movement away from a crack tip
The W-Cu system can be formulated as a high-entropy alloy processable by L-PBF
This L-PBF W-Cu HEA will outperform conventional W-Cu materials in mechanical durability and thermal transport
